title: Proof Over Theory
paragraphs: I checked into the inn where I planned to stay and then went to confirm Father’s inn. Surprisingly, it was quite close. If I shouted in a tavern, he might be able to hear me.
After confirming Father’s lodging, I casually walked through the capital toward Ren’s location. But before I knew it, some pigs had sniffed me out. I’ll just say something random to throw them off.
“Where have you been? We’ve been looking for you!”
“Bububu—!”

They’re saying something, but I have no idea what. Not that they actually looked for me even one bit. Anyway, everything is falling into place. The Crimson Swine should receive word of where I booked my inn soon. Which means he’ll definitely show up at the inn’s tavern. Now, I need to find Ren. Last time, he said he booked an inn not in the capital but in a village two stops away. That’s a bit of a distance—I should hurry. Shaking off the pigs tailing me, I made my way to the village.
“Finally found you!”
“Huh? Motoyasu?”

By the time I finally found Ren, the sun had already set. I had gone to the inn where he was supposed to be staying, but he wasn’t there. For a moment, I thought I had been tricked, but some people who seemed to be his party members were there, along with some smoked meat. I asked them where Ren was. Turns out, he was still fighting some rather strong plant-type monsters even after nightfall. I couldn’t help but be exasperated.
“What’s up? Why’d you come all the way here?”
“To explain that, I need to follow a certain process.”
“What are you talking about?”
“First—”
I sent Ren a party invite.
“What’s with you all of a sudden? Heroes aren’t supposed to fight together, right? We cancel each other’s experience gain.”
“I’m not here to hunt. I need you to come with me.”
“Why?”
“It’s information… that you’d be better off knowing.”
I could just tell him everything now, but seeing is believing. I want him to witness the truth for himself.
“Well, whatever. I was about to take a break anyway.”
Ren accepted the invitation without resistance. Alright!
“Then let’s go. Portal Spear!”
“What?”
In an instant, we teleported to the front of the inn where Itsuki was staying in Melromarc.
“A teleportation skill? You shouldn’t be able to learn that for a long time—how can you use it?”
“I promise I’ll explain later, but now isn’t the time. I need you to wait here for a moment.”
“Well… I guess that’s fine.”
I peeked into the inn’s tavern to confirm that Itsuki was inside. Now, how should I call him over? Just as I was thinking that, my eyes met with Itsuki’s.
I beckon him over for now. Itsuki, without hesitation, comes over alone. This is quite fortunate.
“Oh? Motoyasu-san, and even Ren-san. What brings you here?”
“Yeah, I was surprised too when Motoyasu suddenly brought me here.”
“Huh… By the way, Ren-san or Motoyasu-san, were either of you near the forest where I was hunting?”
“I was just following my hunting plan from yesterday, so I wouldn’t know.”
“More importantly, I need you to come with me for a bit.”

My response makes Itsuki frown slightly, but he doesn’t make a fuss. The Itsuki from the previous loop probably would have gotten angry. It seems that both Ren and Itsuki are still reasonable at this stage. Oh, Itsuki’s party members are heading this way.
“I need to discuss something privately with just the Heroes.”
“What is this about?”
“Yeah, is this something we can’t just talk about here?”
“They say seeing is believing. I figured it would be faster for both Ren and Itsuki to see for themselves.”
“Huh?”
“I don’t know what you’re up to, but if you explain how, you learned a teleportation skill, I’ll go along with it.”
“Teleportation skill?”

Ren and Itsuki are quite cooperative at this point. Ren whispers to Itsuki that I used a teleportation skill to bring him here. When Itsuki hears that I can already use the Portal skill at this stage, his eyes widen in shock.
“Follow me, and I’ll explain.”
“Alright.”
“Fine. It doesn’t seem like a bad deal.”
Itsuki tells his party that he’ll be stepping out for a bit to socialize with the other Heroes, then leaves the tavern.
“So, what now?”

I take a roundabout route toward the inn where Father is staying. That inn has a tavern too, but that’s not my destination. I also need to be careful not to run into the Crimson Swine, as that would be dangerous.
“We’re almost there.”
“Where exactly are you taking us?”

Just in case, I take a detour through the backstreets and discreetly chant Liberation Fire Flasher to lure out any hidden pursuers and burn them away. That should physically eliminate any prying eyes.
“What was that? Looked like something just flashed…”
Most likely, those who were tailing us just went up in flames. As expected, someone was spying on us. But right now, I don’t want to give Ren and Itsuki any unnecessary information.
“Well, this is a back alley, so that makes sense, but isn’t the security bad considering the world is in crisis?”
“I see, so it’s as dangerous as you’d expect from another world.”
“In games, towns are usually peaceful, right?”
“Because they’re safe zones… But yeah, thinking about it realistically, bad security means rough types are bound to appear.”
“It’s fine.”

If anything happens, I’ll take care of it myself. As we talk, we approach the inn where Father is staying. …There are soldiers patrolling in a strangely unnatural way. That’s bound to raise suspicion.
“Ren, Itsuki, excuse me for a moment.”
“Huh? Whoa!”
“Wha—”
Grabbing onto Ren and Itsuki’s collars, I leap high into the air and land on the roof of a building. I make sure to put them down carefully so they don’t get hurt.
“What the hell!?”
“Shhh… If you’re loud, the guards will notice us.”
“Notice us? What are we even being cautious of? What’s ahead?”
“Fa—I mean, Naofumi’s inn.”
“Huh? You’re calling Naofumi too?”
“Well… We’re all Heroes, so of course. But more importantly, how did you just grab us and jump onto a roof like that?”
“I’ll explain that step by step as well.”

The two of them eye me suspiciously, but whether they sense I’m not lying or just realize there’s something more going on, they silently follow along. And then… we reach the rooftop of the inn where Father is staying. From this point on, things get a bit more complicated. Using my spear, I carefully create an opening in the roof without making a sound.
“We’re going in through here.”
“Why the hell do we have to do this?”
“Can you just explain already? If we’re here to talk to Naofumi, this isn’t necessary, is it?”
“We’re not here to talk to Naofumi.”
“Huh?”
Itsuki furrows his brows. Well, to be fair, it probably does seem like I’m dragging them into some sort of crime. But this is all part of the necessary steps.
“Itsuki, I don’t know what Motoyasu is planning, but let’s just follow him. It seems like there’s a reason for all this.”
“…Alright.”
Ren and Itsuki obediently enter the ceiling crawlspace of the inn. I go in last and carefully cover up the hole.
“Fast Fire.”

I use a small fire spell to dimly illuminate the space as we quietly move above the ceiling toward the room where Father is staying. Since we’re crouching, Ren and Itsuki seem like they’re about to make noise, so I chant All Liberation Fire Mirage X to muffle any sound.
“Alright…”
I create three small holes in the ceiling to peek into the room. Inside, Father is relaxing, taking off his chainmail.
“Naofumi-san is just resting, isn’t he?”
Itsuki whispers to me. Ren seems to be thinking the same thing.
Maybe we got here too soon? I thought it would be cutting it close, but…
“Just wait a little longer.”
“Look, we didn’t come here to play ninja with you, Motoyasu.”

Just as they start complaining, Father places some silver coins behind his shield before lying down to sleep. Oh yeah, in the first world, he threw silver coins at me, and he had them in the previous loop as well. As expected, he must have been keeping them hidden behind his shield.
“See? Now Naofumi-san’s asleep.”
“I’d like to get some rest myself…”
“I was planning to spend more time with my party, I say.”
“…If you complain too much, I’ll make sure you stay put—by force, if necessary.”
Annoyed by their grumbling, I let a bit of killing intent seep into my voice. They immediately freeze up in fear.
Good. Hopefully, by now, they’ve started to realize just how strong I am.
